# Fog

#### Exponential Height Fog { #unreal-heightfog }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFog_i0a</code></dd></div></dl>

Place UE's Exponential Height Fog in the scene, as an Exponential Height Fog actor in a level. Turn on Volumetric Fog for lit, shadowed fog (light shafts); the Path Tracer renders the fog only with Volumetric Fog on. Lights scatter into it by their Volumetric Scattering Intensity.

Height of the fog actor, in scene units along the stage's up axis: the fog's density is Fog Density there and grows below it.

## Inscattering Texture

#### Inscattering Color Cubemap { #unreal-heightfog-inscatteringcolorcubemap }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>(empty)</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:InscatteringColorCubemap</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogInscatteringColorCubemap_l4bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Cubemap that can be specified for fog color, which is useful to make distant, heavily fogged scene elements match the sky. When the cubemap is specified, FogInscatteringColor is ignored and Directional inscattering is disabled. Path of a cooked asset in the runtime project (/Game/... or /Engine/...).

## Directional Inscattering

#### Directional Inscattering Exponent { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringexponent }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>4</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>2 to 64</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringExponent</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringExponent_zgcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the size of the directional inscattering cone, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored and the volumetric fog Scattering Distribution is used instead.

#### Directional Inscattering Start Distance { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>10000</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringStartDistance_4ocj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the start distance from the viewer of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - There must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

#### Directional Inscattering Color { #unreal-heightfog-directionalinscatteringluminance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:DirectionalInscatteringLuminance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogDirectionalInscatteringLuminance_micj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Controls the color of the directional inscattering, which is used to approximate inscattering from a directional light. Note: - there must be a directional light with bUsedAsAtmosphereSunLight enabled for DirectionalInscattering to be used. - When r.SupportExpFogMatchesVolumetricFog = 1, this value is ignored.

## Volumetric Fog

#### Volumetric Fog { #unreal-heightfog-benablevolumetricfog }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bEnableVolumetricFog</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbEnableVolumetricFog_2xbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Whether to enable Volumetric fog. Scalability settings control the resolution of the fog simulation. Note that Volumetric fog currently does not support StartDistance, FogMaxOpacity and FogCutoffDistance. Volumetric fog also can't match exponential height fog in general as exponential height fog has non-physical behavior.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-volumetric"></div>

#### Scattering Distribution { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogscatteringdistribution }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.2</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>-0.9 to 0.9</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogScatteringDistribution</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogScatteringDistribution_incj</code></dd></div></dl>

Controls the scattering phase function - how much incoming light scatters in various directions. A distribution value of 0 scatters equally in all directions, while .9 scatters predominantly in the light direction. In order to have visible volumetric fog light shafts from the side, the distribution will need to be closer to 0.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-scattering-distribution"></div>

#### Albedo { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogalbedo }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1, 1, 1</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogAlbedo</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogAlbedo_gwbj</code></dd></div></dl>

The height fog particle reflectiveness used by volumetric fog. Water particles in air have an albedo near white, while dust has slightly darker value.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-albedo"></div>

#### Emissive { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogemissive }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0, 0, 0</code></dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogEmissive</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogEmissive_pzbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Light emitted by height fog. This is a density so more light is emitted the further you are looking through the fog. In most cases skylight is a better choice, however right now volumetric fog does not support precomputed lighting, So stationary skylights are unshadowed and static skylights don't affect volumetric fog at all.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-emissive"></div>

#### Extinction Scale { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogextinctionscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0.1 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogExtinctionScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogExtinctionScale_3bcj</code></dd></div></dl>

Scales the height fog particle extinction amount used by volumetric fog. Values larger than 1 cause fog particles everywhere absorb more light.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="fog-extinction-scale"></div>

#### View Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>6000</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>1000 to 10000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogDistance_pzbj</code></dd></div></dl>

Distance over which volumetric fog should be computed, after the start distance. Larger values extend the effect into the distance but expose under-sampling artifacts in details.

#### Start Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogstartdistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 5000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStartDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStartDistance_u7bj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance from the camera that the volumetric fog will start, in world units.

<div class="hdue-figure" data-figure="ref-volumetric-fog-start-distance"></div>

#### Near Fade In Distance { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfognearfadeindistance }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1000</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogNearFadeInDistance_zgcj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

Distance over which volumetric fog will fade in from the start distance.

#### Static Lighting Scattering Intensity { #unreal-heightfog-volumetricfogstaticlightingscatteringintensity }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 10</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:VolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensity</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogVolumetricFogStaticLightingScatteringIntensity_f5cj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span></dl>

#### Override Light Colors With Fog Inscattering Colors { #unreal-heightfog-boverridelightcolorswithfoginscatteringcolors }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbOverrideLightColorsWithFogInscatteringColors_s3cj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Whether to use FogInscatteringColor for the Sky Light volumetric scattering color and DirectionalInscatteringColor for the Directional Light scattering color. Make sure your directional light has 'Atmosphere Sun Light' enabled! Enabling this allows Volumetric fog to better match Height fog in the distance, but produces non-physical volumetric lighting that may not match surface lighting.

## Fog Screen Space Scattering - EXPERIMENTAL

#### Enable Fog Screen Space Scattering { #unreal-heightfog-benablefsss }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bEnableFSSS</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbEnableFSSS_fjbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Enable FSSS (Fog Screen Space Scattering) to approximate multiple scattering.

#### Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale { #unreal-heightfog-fsssscenecolorscatteringamountscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountScale_incj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

The amount of scene color injected into the fog screen space scattering technique. When 0, only the fog luminance will be scattered. When 1, fog and scene luminance will be scattered. When above 1, more scene color can be injected to increase the brightness of the multiple scattering effect, even when the fog is not too intense. We cannot scatter more than the scene color however.

#### Scene Color Scattering Amount Power { #unreal-heightfog-fsssscenecolorscatteringamountpower }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 2</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSceneColorScatteringAmountPower_incj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

Apply a power over the amount of scattered scene luminance after it is evaluated using Scene Color Scattering Amount Scale. A value smaller than 1 can show more scattering where the fog is less intense.

#### Spread Scale { #unreal-heightfog-fsssspreadscale }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.1</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSSpreadScale</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSSpreadScale_xpbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

The scale of the spread for the fog multiple scattering. This basically scales mip level sampled from the blurred screen space FSSS texture. Increasing will make scene and thicker fog look fuzzier. But too high values can cause artifacts such as halos around depth discontinuities.

#### Blur Control { #unreal-heightfog-fsssblurcontrol }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd><code>0.5</code></dd></div><div><dt>Range</dt><dd>0 to 1</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:FSSSBlurControl</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogFSSSBlurControl_xpbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Realtime only</span><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

When generating the the blurred screen space FSSS texture, this controls how much of the blurred lower mip levels is injected back into the sharper higher mip levels. A higher value will result in a blurrier result. But when = 1, multiple scattering will be a single average color of the FSSS texture.

## Rendering

#### Holdout { #unreal-heightfog-bholdout }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>Off</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bHoldout</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbHoldout_jebj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If this is True, this primitive will render black with an alpha of 0, but all secondary effects (shadows, reflections, indirect lighting) remain. This feature requires activating the project setting(s) "Alpha Output", and "Support Primitive Alpha Holdout" if using the deferred renderer.

#### Render In Main Pass { #unreal-heightfog-brenderinmainpass }

<dl class="hdue-facts"><div><dt>Default</dt><dd>On</dd></div><div><dt>USD attribute</dt><dd><code>unreal:heightFog:bRenderInMainPass</code></dd></div><div><dt>Houdini parameter</dt><dd><code>xn__unrealheightFogbRenderInMainPass_6sbj</code></dd></div><span class="hdue-badge">Advanced</span></dl>

If true, this component will be rendered in the main pass (basepass, transparency)
